VERDICT: CHALLENGE C0031 | `scan_health()` creates a fresh local `tools_available = {}` on every call and has no persistent memory of prior unavailability. The proposed fix says “skip tools already marked unavailable in tools_available”, but that dict is populated only after each runner executes within the same call, so there is nothing to skip. This is not a real bug in the current implementation.

VERDICT: CHALLENGE C0033 | The severity mapping in `run_bandit()` is internally consistent with the module’s own severity schema (`ToolDiagnostic.severity` is `"error" | "warning" | "info"`), and `counts_by_severity` is only an aggregate counter, not a decision engine. Re-mapping LOW→warning and MEDIUM→error would be arbitrary inflation, not a correctness fix.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.96
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `EndocrineLayer.run()` returns an `EndocrineReport` containing `fix_evaluations`, but `bench/insect_brain.py` exposes no endocrine integration point at all. There is no `endocrine_report` field on `BrainState` or `RoundRecord`, no import of `EndocrineReport`, and no method that accepts or persists endocrine output. This contradicts the endocrine docstring claim “Assembled by EndocrineLayer.report() and handed to the insect brain” and the task statement that endocrine pacing/health signals guide round decisions. Evidence in context: `EndocrineLayer.run()` produces the report; `InsectBrain` never consumes it.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer’s core outputs are effectively dead at the system boundary: health scan, fix evaluation verdicts, and pacing signals may run, but the insect brain cannot receive, persist, or act on them. For PoC goals, this means the advertised “whole-body health monitor” feature does not fire end-to-end; reviewers would be misled into thinking endocrine feedback affects orchestration when it currently cannot.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Add a minimal integration slot in `InsectBrain`, e.g. `self.endocrine_report: Optional[EndocrineReport] = None`, and have the orchestrator assign the report there between rounds. No extra processing is needed; just make the interface exist so the feature can actually be handed off.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.90
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_count_tool_issues()` is annotated and documented to accept a single `file_path: str`, but `run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, and `run_bandit` all require `List[str]`. The function currently calls `tool_runner([file_path])`, so the implementation is correct, but the interface contract is wrong. This is not just notation: the same helper is reused as the abstraction boundary for fix evaluation, and its current signature invites future callers to pass a list or alternative scope incorrectly. The mismatch is visible directly in the function definition versus the runner signatures.
FOLLOW: This helper is central to fix evaluation. A misleading contract at this boundary increases the chance of future regressions where callers pass already-listified paths or assume single-file semantics while tool runners have project-scope behavior. Because fix evaluation already has multiple scope/path bugs, this incorrect helper contract compounds maintenance risk and can reintroduce silently wrong verdicts.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Change `_count_tool_issues` to accept `paths: List[str]` and pass `tool_runner(paths)` directly, updating call sites accordingly.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `run_mypy()` drops valid mypy diagnostics when column numbers are absent. Its regex hard-requires `file:line:col: severity: message`, but mypy commonly emits `file:line: error: ...` without a column, depending on message type/options. The current parser therefore undercounts or returns zero diagnostics for valid output forms. Evidence: the compiled pattern is `^(.+?):(\d+):(\d+):\s+(error|warning|note): ...$`, making the `:(\d+)` column segment mandatory.
FOLLOW: Health scans and fix evaluations can silently miss mypy findings, causing `counts_by_tool["mypy"]`, `total`, and category aggregates to be wrong. Because the module presents itself as mechanically extracting metrics, silently discarding a normal mypy output format produces misleading health reports and can falsely mark fixes as harmless.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Make the column group optional in the regex and set `column=0` when absent.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.79
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` can emit a false `novelty_plateau` when `round_idx` and `novelty_counts` are inconsistent. The code comments say they “should track 1:1 with rounds”, but the actual guard only checks `len(novelty_counts) >= 3 and round_idx >= 2`, then uses `recent = novelty_counts[-3:]` regardless of whether the latest list entry corresponds to `round_idx`. If the caller passes stale or extra history, the function silently evaluates the wrong rounds.
FOLLOW: A stale plateau signal can cause premature convergence checking or relay degradation decisions at the wrong time. In PoC terms this can make the pacing feature fire, but on the wrong evidence, misleading reviewers about convergence behavior.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — Require exact alignment before evaluating: only run the plateau check when `len(novelty_counts) == round_idx + 1`; otherwise skip emitting the signal.
VERIFIED: TRUE
